programme: A nuclear-receptor lipid-sensing checkpoint on IL-17-producing T cells: RORA and NR1H3 (LXRα) are oxysterol/lipid-responsive nuclear receptors that sit upstream of IL17A transcription (RORA and GFI1 both list IL17A directly as a target), PPARA is a fatty-acid-sensing nuclear receptor in the same family that co-regulates the metabolic state of these cells, and GFI1 is the hematopoietic transcription factor that gates T-cell/myeloid lineage output (IL7R, CSF1R, CSF3, ITGAE) feeding into the same IL-17 checkpoint.
role_in_a: In multiple sclerosis this nuclear-receptor/lipid-sensing module is expected to set the threshold for pathogenic Th17 differentiation among CNS-infiltrating T cells; NR1H3 carries direct genetic support as an MS risk locus that regulates its own expression (PMID 29801879), and GFI1 sits in an MS-associated regulatory network (PMID 31482761), consistent with a lineage/lipid checkpoint upstream of IL-17 output rather than a bystander signature.
role_in_b: In psoriasis the same family of receptors is expected to tune keratinocyte lipid barrier state and the local IL-17 inflammatory tone that defines lesional plaques; PPARA is directly implicated by differential receptor expression in lesional versus non-lesional psoriatic skin (PMID 41699832), the tissue and disease context in which IL-17 blockade is now standard care.
shared_axis: MS and psoriasis are both diseases in which IL-17-producing T cells are pathogenic, and RORA/NR1H3/PPARA are the nuclear receptors that sense lipid/oxysterol state to license or restrain that IL-17 programme, with GFI1 acting as the upstream lineage gate on the same IL17A target — so the same lipid-sensing checkpoint could independently tip Th17 output toward the CNS in one disease and the skin in the other.
reasoning: The module is nameable and internally consistent (nuclear receptors converging on an IL17A target shared with GFI1), and two of its four members are independently placed in each respective disease by retrieved papers, but no retrieved source states the MS–psoriasis connection itself — that link rests on general Th17/IL-17 biology, not on anything in the record, which is exactly what moderate strength means. RORA's inclusion is architecturally central (it is the literal IL17A regulator) but has no retrieved paper support in either disease, so the claim leans on target-list structure plus recurrence (119/208) rather than literature.
support: PMID 29801879 — NR1H3 genetic variants regulate its own expression and confer multiple sclerosis risk. PMID 41699832 — PPARA-family (endocannabinoid) receptor expression differs between lesional and non-lesional psoriatic skin. PMID 31482761 — GFI1 falls within an integrated multiple sclerosis genetics/disease network.
how_to_falsify: In paired CD4+ T cells from CNS lesions (or CSF) of MS patients and skin-infiltrating T cells from psoriatic plaques, measure RORA, NR1H3, PPARA and GFI1 expression alongside IL17A transcript; if modulating these receptors pharmacologically (e.g., LXR or PPARα agonism, RORα/γt inverse agonism) fails to shift IL17A output concordantly across both tissue types, the shared lipid-sensing checkpoint account is wrong.
caveats: Brain–skin tissue pairing over 208 patient-group comparisons drawn from 6 independent cohort pairs; recurrence fractions for the four carrying factors range from 119/208 (RORA) to 144/208 (PPARA), so this is not a uniformly high-confidence set. The usual PGC1 coactivator partners of this receptor family (PPARGC1A, PPARGC1B) appeared only as single-view hits and did not recur, so the account is built on the receptors alone, not a documented receptor–coactivator complex. NR3C1 (glucocorticoid receptor) was screened out as tissue-generic, which argues the RORA/NR1H3/PPARA signal is not simply 'nuclear receptors are generic here.' Eight other concordant factors (NR2F1, WT1, POU3F4, POU4F2, EGR1, MTF2, EBF2, FOXA2) were left out of the programme because they do not connect to this axis or to each other in the record, and no attempt is made here to explain them.
